title: The room and the outside world
description: What reaches the log from outside the conversation's own turns. The LiveKit room's facts, as the room reports them: it opened, who joined and with which attributes, who left, who is speaking, which tracks they publish. And the facts that cross the room's edge: what the outside world hands the agent (an event from the tenant's backend or from a participant) and what the agent hands a browser. The agent never touches LiveKit; it reads these facts. Each is one event under events/.

RoomOpened.description: The LiveKit room exists and the call lives in it. Phone and web calls have one; a text session has no room and never logs this.

name.description: The room's name, the one a browser or a SIP leg joins: call-CA_8f4a2c.

sid.description: livekit's id for the room, for tracing in its logs.

ParticipantJoined.description: Somebody joined the room: the caller over SIP or the widget, the agent, a supervisor, a listener, or a second SIP leg. Their attributes travel verbatim: the caller's number is a fact of the room, not a field we invent.

identity.description: The identity the room knows them by: sip_+34600123456 for a SIP caller, agent-AJ_5d2e8f for the agent, a visitor id for the widget.

name.description: Their display name, when the room carried one.

attributes.description: livekit's participant attributes, string to string, exactly as the room holds them. For a SIP leg that is sip.callID, sip.callStatus, sip.trunkID, sip.trunkPhoneNumber, sip.phoneNumber, sip.ruleID and one sip.h.<header> per SIP header the trunk lets through; for the agent, lk.agent.state. Never renamed, never summarised; the public projection drops them whole.

ParticipantLeft.description: Somebody left the room. When it is the caller, call.ended follows.

reason.description: Why, as livekit's DisconnectReason names it, in lower case: client_initiated (they hung up or closed the tab), participant_removed (a participant.remove), room_closed, sip_trunk_failure, connection_timeout, and whatever the library adds next. Open on purpose: a reason the room reports is a fact even before this schema has heard of it.

ParticipantSpeaking.description: The room's own voice activity for one participant flipped. Ephemeral: it is a light for the console, and the turns say who spoke.

speaking.description: True when they started, false when they stopped.

TrackPublished.description: A participant put a track on the room: their microphone, their camera, a screen.

TrackUnpublished.description: A participant's track left the room: they stopped sharing, or a participant.mute took their audio away.

EventReceived.description: A fact arrived from outside the conversation: the tenant's backend sent call.event, or a participant's browser sent pinecall.event. One event for both, told apart by source. It reached the log only because the agent declared the name in its events, from that source; anything else was refused before this.

name.description: The event's name, dotted, as the agent declared it: slot.released, form.submitted.

data.description: Whatever came with it, as JSON. The app reads it; the platform never does.

identity.description: The participant that sent it, for source participant. Absent when the app did.

RoomSent.description: The agent pushed a payload to a browser in the room, on the tenant's room.send. Ephemeral, and the payload stays out of the log: the tenant chose what to send and to whom.

topic.description: The DataChannel topic it went out on: pinecall.ui for the widget, or a topic of the tenant's own.

to.description: The identity it was addressed to. Absent: every participant in the room.

bytes.description: How many bytes the payload was.
